prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse room layout: the wooden floor extends ahead, with walls, doorways, and furniture forming nearer bright regions and farther dark regions; without metric calibration, the floor and walls appear roughly 1–4 m from the camera wearer. Across frames 1–3, a chair and nearby furniture lie mainly left or ahead-left at approximately 1–2 m, while the open floor and rear parts of the room are farther away; the changing depth boundaries indicate camera translation and turning rather than a stable straight view. In frames 4–5, the person and the camera wearer’s foreground arm or carried object become bright, placing them within roughly 0.3–1.5 m, with the foreground item partly occluding the person and floor; the person is to the right/front and appears closer by frame 5. This map makes near/far layering and otherwise subtle wall/floor boundaries clearer than RGB, but distances are only rough: large dark areas, smeared silhouettes, abrupt frame-edge changes, and similar brightness across differently placed surfaces make it unreliable for precise measurements or gaze direction.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies a chair in the second frame at the upper-left/left-front of the camera wearer and a person in the fifth frame across the right and lower-right; their RGB positions suggest the chair is roughly 1–2 m away and the person roughly 0.5–1.5 m away. The person mask extends partly beyond the bottom and right image boundaries and is interrupted by irregular edges, indicating partial visibility and occlusion by foreground arms or objects; the chair is also fragmented and partly out of the upper frame. Relative to the camera wearer, the detected person is in front-right and close enough to be near arm’s reach, whereas no reliable person mask is provided in frame 4 even though RGB and pose evidence show a person there. The map makes object identity and occupied image regions clearer than RGB, but it misses most furniture, walls, the floor, hands, and the person in earlier frames, so it cannot reliably establish complete inter-object distances, facing direction, gaze, or motion across all five frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects a small cluster of body keypoints only in frame 4, located ahead-right and above the lower foreground, corresponding to the nearby person visible in RGB at roughly 1–2 m from the camera wearer. The keypoint arrangement indicates a partially visible, obliquely oriented upper body rather than a clear frontal skeleton, so the person may be turned partly sideways, but head orientation and whether they look toward the camera wearer are not reliably recoverable. The cluster’s position relative to the camera wearer’s foreground arm or object suggests close proximity, approximately at the edge of arm’s reach, while much of the body is occluded or outside the detected region; no magenta hand skeletons appear. Pose makes sparse body location and articulation cues easier to isolate than RGB, but missing limbs, absent detections in the other four frames, and several disconnected points make approach, retreat, exact facing, person-to-object distances, and five-frame motion unreliable.
